ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 2106 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported five major and about seventy-five minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.62; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Mr. van der Luyden addressed Archer with a female term (‘cô’); now ‘cậu’.
‘Our cousin’ is the Duke, but the draft made it a female cousin; corrected.
‘Episcopalian’ was rendered with the Methodist term; now the Episcopal Church.
‘Husband of Ellen Olenska’s cousin’ read as Ellen’s own husband; corrected.
‘Don’t you always know what to say?’ became a question that inverted the sense; corrected.

The first slice used ‘chàng’ for Archer and ‘nàng’ for May and Ellen while the other slices used ‘anh’, ‘cô’ and ‘bà’; unified across the book (the epithets ‘nàng Cassandra’ and ‘nàng Pocahontas’ were kept).
‘The tribe’ is rendered ‘bộ tộc’ in some places and ‘bộ lạc’ in the glossary.
The register of ‘hắn’ in units 636–659 is rougher than the surrounding narration.

summary: Full assessment of all 2,106 English/Vietnamese passages: two book headings, thirty-four chapter headings and every paragraph. The first reviews scored 8.50, 8.375, 8.80, 8.80, 8.73, 8.50 and 8.65 across seven ranges and found five majors (an address form that was female for a man, a wrong referent for ‘our cousin’, an Episcopalian written as a Methodist, a husband assigned to the wrong woman, and an inverted question); one round of fixes and fresh separate-context blind reviews of the four failing ranges then scored 8.88 (units 1–235), 8.80 (236–447), 8.80 (1428–1709) and 8.80 (1710–2106), with the other three already passing at 8.80, 8.80 and 8.73, and no major or critical finding open. The pronoun system was also unified (anh, cô, bà instead of the draft’s ‘chàng’ and ‘nàng’). The final score is taken from the weakest range, 8.725 on the half-point scale, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. A few minor points remain open.

title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Thời đại ngây thơ’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.
